verdict.rationale: Greptile's first-party docs describe deploying the product in your own infrastructure. Docker Compose covers up to 100 developers and Kubernetes handles 100+ with high availability, with support for AWS, GCP, Azure, air-gapped environments, self-hosted or bring-your-own LLMs, and logs kept only on customer servers. A community request for a self-hosted option predates this and is not a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment, and documentation of licensing or plan requirements for self-hosting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Deploy Greptile in your own infrastructure with Docker Compose. Supports AWS, GCP, Azure, air-gapped environments, and custom LLM configurations.
Kubernetes: 100+ developers. Horizontal scaling, high availability.
Note that in the self-hosted service, logs are stored on customer servers only.
For CI or self-hosted deployments, use an API key
